question: Does a suspended execute time out in the ChatGPT built-in browser, and after how long?
clientError: Error: Timed out running CDP command "Runtime.evaluate" for tab 1
client: ChatGPT desktop built-in browser, model 5.6 Sol
method: probe_hang returns a Promise that never settles. The agent was told not to give up on its own initiative and to report what the client did.
consequence: SELECTS THE HANDSHAKE AS THE CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT — and that is the strongest thing this file supports (R-44). A human cannot review a report and sign it in 22 seconds, so S5 builds toward the two-call handshake: execute returns {status:'awaiting_signature', ticket} immediately and the signature arrives on a separate call. RISK.md already required both modes behind one switch, so this is a switch position, not a rewrite. WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT SUPPORT: 'decisive', 'it times out every time', or any remote-origin claim. ONE run, ON LOCALHOST. It does not separate a WebMCP client timeout from a CDP evaluation-wrapper timeout, does not show the underlying execute() was cancelled, and does not carry to a remote origin — V6-consent-gate is the standing proof that this client behaves differently there. V4's node wants two runs compared at 20 percent by harness/compare-runs.mjs; neither run file nor the comparator exists, so THE NODE HAS NOT PASSED and contingencies[4] is PROVISIONALLY SELECTED, not fired.
incidental: The error names Runtime.evaluate, so this client drives tool execution over CDP via Runtime.evaluate rather than the CDP WebMCP domain's invokeTool. Recorded as an observation, not a conclusion about other clients.
caveat: Measured once, on localhost. The plan requires two independent runs with a disagreement threshold; this is run 1 of 2.
